desc: On 13 November 2024 at 11:30 am in 2154 Rayburn, the House Oversight Committee's Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation and its Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs held a joint hearing chaired by Rep. Nancy Mace, published by GPO as Serial No. 118-135 (CHRG-118hhrg57440). The witnesses were retired Rear Adm. Tim Gallaudet, former Oceanographer of the Navy and former acting NOAA administrator; Luis Elizondo, former Defense Department official; Michael Gold, former NASA associate administrator for space policy and partnerships and a member of the NASA UAP Independent Study Team; and Michael Shellenberger, founder of Public. This is the hearing at which the Immaculate Constellation report entered the Congressional Record: Mace announced from the dais that committee staff had asked her to enter 'this 12-page document that Michael Shellenberger brought today that describes the Immaculate Constellation government program', and it appears in the Index of Documents as 'Report, Pentagon, Immaculate Constellation; submitted by Rep. Mace.' It is also the hearing at which Elizondo answered Mace's direct question - 'Has the government conducted secret UAP crash retrieval programs? Yes or no?' - with a single word, 'Yes', while declining to discuss whether he was read into such programmes except in closed session. Gallaudet testified about the January 2015 Fleet Forces Command 'urgent safety of flight issue' email containing the GIMBAL video, which was recalled from Navy inboxes. Gold cited Alex Dietrich by name, saying she 'was mocked by her colleagues' and that her incident 'went years without any investigation.' Mace also stated on the record that 'there are certain individuals who did not want this hearing to happen because they feared what might be disclosed', and never named them. The hearing's structural achievement was to move the crash-retrieval allegation from a single whistleblower's second-hand account in 2023 to an affirmative one-word answer from a second former official in 2024, and to place a named alleged special access programme into the permanent record of Congress - where, twenty-one months later, no executive branch office has answered for it.

claims.text: The hearing 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth' was held 13 November 2024 at 11:30 a.m. in 2154 Rayburn House Office Building, jointly by the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation and the Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs.

The four witnesses were Dr. Tim Gallaudet (Rear Admiral, USN Ret., CEO of Ocean STL Consulting LLC), Luis Elizondo (author and former DoD official), Michael Gold (former NASA Associate Administrator for Space Policy and Partnerships and member of the NASA UAP Independent Study Team), and Michael Shellenberger (founder of Public).

Luis Elizondo testified: 'UAP are real. Advanced technologies not made by our Government – or any other government – are monitoring sensitive military installations around the globe. Furthermore, the U.S. is in possession of UAP technologies, as are some of our adversaries.'
Elizondo testified: 'In my last position, I managed a Special Access Program on behalf of the White House and the National Security Council.'

Elizondo testified that 'the Pentagon's very own Public Affairs Office openly employs a professional psychological operations officer as the singular point of contact for any UAP-related inquiries from citizens and the media.'

Gallaudet testified that in January 2015, as Commander of Naval Meteorology and Oceanography Command, he received an email on the Navy's secure network from the Fleet Forces Command operations officer with the subject line 'URGENT SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE' attaching the 'Go Fast' video, and that 'the very next day, the email disappeared from my account and those of the other recipients without explanation.'

Gallaudet testified: 'I concluded that the UAP information must have been classified within a special access program managed by an intelligence agency — a compartmented program that even senior officials, including myself, were not read into.'

Gallaudet testified that during a 2024 meeting with the then-acting AARO director and his senior staff he 'was the object of an hours-long influence operation' aimed at validating AARO's historical records report, questioning the USS Nimitz 'tic tac' encounter, and disparaging former government authorities who have spoken publicly about US government UAP programs.

Gallaudet testified that on 11 November 2024 former DoD official Chris Mellon contacted him seeking assistance in sharing with Congress details of a 2017 case involving satellite imagery of UAP 'that has still not been shared with Congress,' and offered to provide the dates in a closed setting.

Shellenberger's written testimony states that a whistleblower report provided to authorised committees of Congress names an active DoD Unacknowledged Special Access Program called IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION which 'serves as a central or parent USAP that consolidates observations' of UAP 'by both tasked and untasked collection platforms,' and that the Executive Branch 'has been managing UAP/NHI issues without Congressional knowledge, oversight, or authorization for some time, quite possibly decades.'
Shellenberger's testimony quotes DoD spokesperson Sue Gough: 'The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called "IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION."'

Shellenberger testified that after publication a source told him the SAP 'is controlled by the White House and executed and administrated by the DOD to avoid compliance with Title 10 of the United States Code,' adding: 'It is essentially a DOD Program, as the White House directed the SECDEF to run it. But that's the loophole.' A former IC official separately told him 'That program is run out of SEC DEF... They don't want to acknowledge it's real.'

The whistleblower report quoted in the testimony concludes that 'the existence of IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION demonstrates the extant capability to detect, quarantine, and transfer UAP and RV [Reproduction Vehicle] collection incidents before they are observed and circulated within the Military Intelligence Enterprise, thus serving as a means of enforcing internal information security.'

Shellenberger's testimony notes that AARO is housed within the Office of the Undersecretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, so 'the office that Congress created to investigate unreported UAP programs is troublingly close to the organizations running the alleged programs,' and that a source warned him that printing the program name 'could trigger government surveillance of me under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.'

The whistleblower report describes an F-22 that 'broke trajectory and attempted to evade but was intercepted and boxed in by approximately 3-6 UAPs,' one of which held station within twelve metres starboard of the cockpit maintaining exact position and orientation through multiple evasive rolls, the aircraft being 'forced out of the mission area under the escort of the UAP formation'; and a carrier incident in which an orange-red sphere descended to 100-200 yards above the flight deck emitting light that 'did not illuminate the ocean or the flight deck of the CVN,' its surface 'roiling like the surface of the sun.'

Gallaudet's testimony asserts a constitutional argument: 'Even the most sensitive Special Access Programs must be reported the Gang of Eight, and all compartmented programs must be reported to the Senate Intelligence Committee. Any and all past failures by DoD and IC components to report UAP programs and activities are not only illegal but would have undermined Congress.'

connections: Chairwoman Nancy Mace (Cybersecurity, IT and Government Innovation) and Chairman Glenn Grothman (National Security, the Border and Foreign Affairs) presided, with Ranking Members Gerald Connolly and Robert Garcia — all four named in each witness's opening address.

IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION is alleged to have been created in 2017 in response to the 16 December 2017 New York Times AATIP article, making that article the causal trigger for a new concealment structure.
The alleged Title 10 evasion — White House direction, SECDEF execution — is a claim about 10 U.S.C. 119 specifically, and about the SAP governance chain set out in DoDD 5205.07.

AARO's placement inside OUSD(I&S) puts the investigating office inside the same organisation that DoDD 5205.07 designates as the primary DoD interface to ODNI and the IC for shared compartmented capabilities.
Chris Mellon's 2017 satellite-imagery case, raised two days before the hearing, is an unresolved thread linking the hearing to national technical means and to whichever agency holds that imagery.

Gallaudet's January 2015 email connects the hearing to the USS Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group pre-deployment exercise and to the 'Go Fast' video, and by extension to Fleet Forces Command's leadership at the time.

Elizondo's account of colleagues giving classified testimony to the DoD and IC Inspectors General links this hearing to the ICIG channel through which David Grusch's 2022 complaint was found credible and urgent.

Michael Gold connects the hearing to NASA (Bill Nelson, Thomas Zurbuchen, Daniel Evans, the UAP Independent Study Team) and to Redwire Space, where he is Chief Growth Officer and where fellow IST member Reggie Brothers sits on the board.
Gallaudet's advisory roles link the hearing to the Sol Foundation, the UAP Disclosure Fund, Harvard's Galileo Project, and Ryan Graves's Americans for Safe Aerospace.
dossier.denialPosture: DoD spokesperson Sue Gough issued a categorical, attributable denial quoted into the hearing record: 'The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION.' The denial is framed as a records statement rather than a factual one, and is exactly the form of denial the alleged White-House-controlled, DoD-executed structure would produce.
dossier.narrative:
The November 2024 hearing was the third in the House Oversight sequence that began with the July 2023 Grusch hearing, and it is the one that matters most structurally, because it moved the argument from 'there are unexplained objects' to 'there is a named program and a named legal evasion.'

Michael Shellenberger's written testimony carries the load. He reported that a current or former US government official acting as a whistleblower had written a report, provided to authorised committees of Congress and their staff, stating that 'the Executive Branch has been managing UAP/NHI issues without Congressional knowledge, oversight, or authorization for some time, quite possibly decades.' The report names an active DoD Unacknowledged Special Access Program, IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION, described by the document's source as a 'strategic intelligence program' that is part of the military's family of long-standing highly-sensitive programs dealing with aspects of the UAP problem. The report states that 'IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION serves as a central or parent USAP that consolidates observations' of UAP 'by both tasked and untasked collection platforms,' and that it 'includes high-quality Imagery Intelligence (IMINT) and Measurement and Signature Intelligence (MASINT) of UAPs,' sourced from a blend of directed and incidental collection in Low Earth Orbit, the upper atmosphere, aviation altitudes and maritime environments. The whistleblower alleges the USAP was created in 2017, after the New York Times published its AATIP story.

The program's stated function, as quoted in the testimony, is the concealment mechanism itself: 'the existence of IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION demonstrates the extant capability to detect, quarantine, and transfer UAP and RV [Reproduction Vehicle] collection incidents before they are observed and circulated within the Military Intelligence Enterprise, thus serving as a means of enforcing internal information security.' That is a claim about a filter operating upstream of the intelligence enterprise, and it is the single most consequential sentence in the hearing record.

The legal mechanism follows. DoD spokesperson Sue Gough issued a categorical denial: 'The DOD has no record, present or historical, of any type of SAP called IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION.' After publication, Shellenberger says a source told him the SAP 'is controlled by the White House and executed and administrated by the DOD to avoid compliance with Title 10 of the United States Code' — 'It is essentially a DOD Program, as the White House directed the SECDEF to run it. But that's the loophole.' A former IC official told him: 'That program is run out of SEC DEF. They don't want to acknowledge it's real.' Shellenberger also notes that AARO is housed within OUSD(I&S), so 'the office that Congress created to investigate unreported UAP programs is troublingly close to the organizations running the alleged programs.' A source warned him that merely printing the program name could trigger FISA surveillance of whoever published it.

The testimony also describes two incidents from the whistleblower's report. An F-22 'broke trajectory and attempted to evade but was intercepted and boxed in by approximately 3-6 UAPs,' with one holding station within twelve metres starboard of the cockpit, 'maintaining its exact position and orientation parallel with the F-22's cockpit despite multiple evasive rolls and maneuvers,' the aircraft then 'forced out of the mission area under the escort of the UAP formation.' Separately, an aircraft carrier's crew observed a 'small orange-red sphere' descend to 100-200 yards above the flight deck, emitting light that 'did not illuminate the ocean or the flight deck of the CVN despite the visual appearance of intense luminosity,' with a surface 'roiling like the surface of the sun.'

Tim Gallaudet's testimony supplies the institutional-deletion evidence. In January 2015, as Commander of Naval Meteorology and Oceanography Command, he received an email on the Navy's secure network from the Fleet Forces Command operations officer, addressed to all subordinate commanders, subject line in capitals: 'URGENT SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE,' attaching what is now the 'Go Fast' video. 'The very next day, the email disappeared from my account and those of the other recipients without explanation,' and neither the Commander of Fleet Forces nor his operations officer ever raised it again. Gallaudet's inference is stated plainly: 'I concluded that the UAP information must have been classified within a special access program managed by an intelligence agency.' He further testified that in 2024 he was the object of an hours-long influence operation by the then-acting AARO director and senior staff, aimed at validating AARO's historical records report, questioning the Nimitz tic tac case, and disparaging former officials who have spoken publicly. He told the committee that on 11 November 2024, two days before the hearing, Chris Mellon had asked for his help getting Congress details of a 2017 case involving satellite imagery of UAP 'that has still not been shared with Congress.'

Luis Elizondo's testimony is the shortest and the most direct: 'UAP are real. Advanced technologies not made by our Government — or any other government — are monitoring sensitive military installations around the globe. Furthermore, the U.S. is in possession of UAP technologies, as are some of our adversaries. I believe we are in the midst of a multi-decade, secretive arms race — one funded by misallocated taxpayer dollars and hidden from our elected representatives and oversight bodies.' He established his standing in the same paragraph: 'In my last position, I managed a Special Access Program on behalf of the White House and the National Security Council.' He described a 'small cadre' inside government that has created 'a culture of suppression and intimidation,' including 'unwarranted criminal investigations, harassment, and efforts to destroy one's credibility,' and stated that many of his former colleagues have given classified testimony to the DoD and Intelligence Community Inspectors General and were subsequently targeted with threats to their careers, clearances 'and even our lives.'

Michael Gold's testimony is the counterweight in tone but not in direction: a former NASA associate administrator arguing that stigma, not evidence, is the binding constraint.

What the record does not settle: no committee has published the underlying Immaculate Constellation report, no dates or units are attached to the F-22 or carrier incidents, and the acting AARO director in Gallaudet's account is not named in his written testimony.
openQuestions: Who is the IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION whistleblower, and did any committee formally obtain and retain the underlying report?
What dates, units and locations attach to the F-22 encounter and the carrier flight-deck sphere described in the report?
Who was the acting AARO director present at the meeting Gallaudet describes as an influence operation, and who were the senior staff?
Was Chris Mellon's 2017 satellite-imagery case ever briefed to the oversight committees, and which agency holds the imagery?
Did DoD's denial address only the exact string 'IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION,' and would a nickname change or an unacknowledged compartment render the denial technically accurate?
Is there a written record of the Fleet Forces Command email Gallaudet describes, and was its deletion a routine recall or a directed action?
dossier.whatItIs: A joint hearing of the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability's Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation and its Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs, titled 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth,' held 13 November 2024 at 11:30 a.m. in 2154 Rayburn House Office Building. The four witnesses were Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet USN (Ret.), Luis Elizondo, Michael Gold, and Michael Shellenberger. Written testimony from all four is published on the committee's website.
dossier.whyImplicated: This is the hearing that entered the name of an alleged active Unacknowledged Special Access Program — IMMACULATE CONSTELLATION — into the congressional record, together with the sourced allegation that the program is controlled by the White House and executed by DoD specifically 'to avoid compliance with Title 10 of the United States Code.' It is also the hearing at which a retired flag officer testified under his own name that a UAP safety-of-flight email was deleted from Navy accounts overnight, and at which a former DoD official who managed a Special Access Program for the White House and NSC testified that 'the U.S. is in possession of UAP technologies.' The same witness testified that the Pentagon's Public Affairs Office employs a psychological operations officer as the single point of contact for UAP inquiries, and another witness described being subjected to an hours-long influence operation by the then-acting AARO director. The hearing converts whistleblower assertions into dated, attributable, congressionally-published documents.

timeline.label: Elizondo's SCIF-signed gag
timeline.text: Elizondo testifies that he signed a US Government document in a SCIF, before a security officer, permitting continued public speech on some topics but barring discussion of crash retrieval. Moskowitz walks him through the signing.

timeline.label: Elizondo corroborates Grusch under oath
timeline.text: Asked by Rep. Burchett whether he agreed the US has run a multi-decade UAP crash, retrieval and reverse engineering program, Luis Elizondo answers 'Yes, sir,' and discloses he worked with Grusch at US Space Force.

timeline.label: Elizondo confirms the blocked contractor transfer on the record
timeline.text: Rep. Burlison reads the Lockheed Martin - Bigelow Aerospace - CIA account into the hearing; Elizondo answers 'What I can say is that it was blocked.' Rep. Mace elicits confirmation that material is allocated to contractors by domain expertise.

timeline.label: 'Immaculate Constellation' document entered into the congressional record
timeline.text: At the joint House Oversight hearing 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth', Chairwoman Mace enters into the record a 12-page Pentagon document describing 'the unacknowledged special access program called Immaculate Constellation', delivered to Congress by witness Michael Shellenberger. Witnesses: Gallaudet, Elizondo, Shellenberger, Gold. Printed as Serial No. 118-135 (CHRG-118hhrg57440).

timeline.label: Sworn testimony before House Oversight
timeline.text: Elizondo answers 'Yes' under oath to secret UAP crash retrieval programs and to their reverse-engineering purpose, and describes 'a culture of suppression and intimidation that I have personally been victim to'.

timeline.label: A programme name enters the Congressional Record
timeline.text: Mace moves the twelve-page report into the record from the dais. Elizondo answers 'Yes' when asked whether the government has conducted secret UAP crash retrieval programs. Mace says certain individuals did not want the hearing to happen and does not name them.

timeline.label: House Oversight hearing: Exposing the Truth
